questions.enonce_markdown:
How significant was the washing of feet of the Apostles in John chapter 13?

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** In John 13:1-20, during the last meal before the Passover, Jesus rises from the table, takes off his outer robe, ties a towel around himself, pours water into a basin and washes the disciples' feet. This act has several levels of significance.

**1. An act of humility and service.** Washing feet was the work of a slave or servant. By performing it, Jesus, whom the disciples call Teacher and Lord, takes the role of a servant. He says, "I have set you an example, that you also should do as I have done to you" (13:15). Leadership in the community is service, and not status. The disciples had shown the opposite attitude elsewhere, for example in disputes over who is greatest (compare Luke 22:24-27).

**2. A sign of his love.** John introduces the scene by saying that Jesus, having loved his own, "loved them to the end" (13:1). The foot-washing is a sign of that love and prepares the new commandment: "love one another as I have loved you" (13:34).

**3. A symbol of cleansing and of his death.** Peter protests, "You will never wash my feet." Jesus answers, "Unless I wash you, you have no share with me" (13:8). This suggests that people must accept what Jesus does for them: his self-giving, ending in the cross, makes them clean. Many Christians see the act as an acted parable of his death for others. Jesus also says "you are clean, though not all of you" (13:10-11), alluding to Judas.

**4. A lesson in understanding.** "You do not know now what I am doing, but later you will understand" (13:7). The meaning becomes clear in the light of the cross and resurrection.

**5. A call to imitation and blessing.** Jesus says that a servant is not greater than the master and "blessed are you if you do them" (13:16-17). In some churches, the foot-washing is observed as a rite at Maundy Thursday; in others it is taken as a model of service.

**Conclusion.** The washing of the feet is significant because it shows the humility and love of Jesus, interprets his death, and sets the standard of service for his followers.
